tabTooltips.basicInfo: A tab to view and edit this goal's basic information, such as the exam name, start date, status, and notes. Use it to rename the goal or correct its start date.
tabTooltips.basicInfoReading: A tab to view and edit this reading goal's basic information, such as the title, start date, status, and notes.
tabTooltips.basicInfoWork: A tab to view and edit this work goal's basic information, such as the project name, start date, status, and notes.
tabTooltips.subjects: A tab to set the exam date and passing score for each subject, for exams split into multiple subjects (such as certifications where each subject has its own exam date or passing score). Use it to add and edit subjects and manage each one's passing criteria.
tabTooltips.materials: A tab to register the materials you use to study (textbooks, workbooks, etc.) and manage their links to subjects, planned cycles, and amounts. Use it to add new materials or set the information used to calculate your daily quota.
tabTooltips.resourceAllocation: A tab to set the time (in minutes) allocated to this goal within each time slot. When you're working on multiple goals at once, allocations are controlled so their total never exceeds the time slot's length, preventing goals from competing for the same slot.
tabTooltips.loadProfile: A tab to set a load coefficient (baseline 1.0) for a specific period, when you want to increase or decrease your daily study volume for that period only. Use it to reduce load during busy periods or increase it during a final push.
tabTooltips.book: A tab to register the title, author, total pages, and target completion date, and check your reading progress (days remaining, last recorded date, current streak, page progress). Total pages is required (to display page progress). When you finish reading, choose "Mark as complete" from the goal detail actions (a finished reading goal is shown as "Finished").
tabTooltips.workAssignment: A tab to register the client, expected work content, start date, team members, and roles, and check your work progress (elapsed days, last recorded date, current streak).
tabTooltips.monthlyReport: A tab to generate a monthly report draft, review and edit it on the spot, and download it as Markdown.
tabTooltips.semiannualReview: A tab to generate a semiannual review report, review and edit it on the spot, and download it as Markdown.
tabTooltips.evaluationReport: A tab to select a registered team member and generate an evaluation report draft based on their daily work records and AI feedback history, then review, edit, and download it. Only shown when your role is set to "Evaluator."

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Instructions for using each screen are gathered here. Use the table of contents or search to jump to what you need.

intro.title: Getting started: how Michinari works
intro.p1: Michinari is an app for planning your study toward a certification exam, recording your daily results, and continuously revising your plan.
intro.p2: The basic flow is as follows: ① Create a goal from "Goals" (type: certification exam, reading, or work) ② Register available study time slots in the study environment settings (used for certification exam and reading resource allocation) ③ Set up the fields for your goal's type on the goal details screen ④ Submit "Today's report" from the dashboard every day ⑤ Check your progress on the calendar or analytics screen ⑥ For certification exams, register your exam results, complete the goal, and export your knowledge; for reading, mark it as finished and export the completion report; for work, mark it as complete.
intro.p3: For detailed instructions on each screen, open the relevant section from the table of contents or search below.

dashboard.title: Dashboard (the screen shown at startup)
dashboard.p1: This is the first screen shown when you open the app. It shows "Today's message" (a short AI-generated message), today's status (not entered / progress only / reported), today's quota, warning banners, goal cards, and summary stats (consecutive days reported, recent report rate, buffer day usage rate, effective speed).
dashboard.p2: The "Today's report" button takes you to the daily report screen. Clicking a warning banner or goal card takes you to that goal's details/edit screen. You can also go to the analytics screen from the stats cards.
dashboard.p3: If you have 2 or more active goals, a goal tab appears at the top of the screen, letting you select one goal at a time (the same approach as the daily report screen). Today's message, warning banners, today's quota, goal cards, and summary stats show only the selected goal's data. Today's status isn't tied to a goal, so it's shared regardless of which goal tab is selected.
dashboard.p4: If you have an active certification exam or reading goal, "This week's recap (by theme)" is also shown. The AI classifies your diary and recall records into multiple themes and automatically builds up each theme's body over time (not available for work). Clicking a theme name takes you to its detail screen, where you can rename the theme, merge it into another theme, or have the AI rebuild its body.

goals.title: Goal list / goal detail editing
goals.p1: The "Goals" screen lists every registered goal. Choosing a type (certification exam, reading, or work) from "Create new goal" lets you create reading and work goals instantly, while certification exam goals use a wizard: pick a preset exam template or enter the exam name directly, then set the exam date, materials, and study hours in order (templates cannot be added or edited). Selecting a goal takes you to its details/edit screen. If you forget how to use the app, or on first launch, you can reopen the welcome screen from the link on the Help screen.
goals.p2: A certification exam goal's detail screen has 5 tabs: "Basic info" (exam name, start date, notes), "Subjects" (subject name, exam date, passing criteria), "Materials" (total amount, planned cycles, subjects covered, due date, required continuous time, required environment, quality metric method), "Resource allocation" (minutes allocated to this goal per time slot), and "Load profile" (load coefficient per period). The load profile and material advanced settings (required continuous time, required environment, quality metric method) are collapsed by default; expand them with "Show advanced settings."
goals.p3: The goal's action area shows "Start," "Pause," "Resume," "Mark as complete," or "Abandon," depending on its status. After completing or abandoning, the goal becomes read-only; a completed or abandoned goal can be reverted with "Resume" to continue it. A certification exam goal cannot be completed until results are in for every subject.
goals.p4: Completed, abandoned, or paused goals can be hidden from the list with "Archive" (view them again with "Show all"). Archived goals, or any goal that isn't currently active, can be permanently erased with "Delete." Deletion cannot be undone and removes all related records and data, so you must type the goal's name to confirm.
goals.p5: A reading goal's detail screen has 3 tabs — "Basic info," "Book," and "Resource allocation" — and doesn't use a daily quota or effective speed. Since reading is also a flexible activity, it's included in the same resource allocation that competes for time slots with certification exams (setting it is optional; you can start without it). Registering the title, author, total pages, and target completion date on the "Book" tab lets you start, and when you finish reading, choose "Mark as complete" from the goal detail actions. The completion report is generated at the same time.
goals.p6: A work goal's detail screen has 4 tabs — "Basic info," "Project info," "Monthly report," and "Semiannual review" — plus an "Evaluation report" tab that appears once you set your role to "Evaluator" on the project info tab (daily quota, effective speed, and resource allocation aren't used). Registering the project name, expected work content, start date, and role on the "Project info" tab lets you start; you can also register, edit, and deactivate team members (name, traits, etc.) from the same tab. The monthly report and semiannual review tabs have the AI generate a draft for the target period, which you can edit on the spot and download as Markdown. The evaluation report tab lets you select a registered member and generate a report draft based on their daily work records and AI feedback history, which you can edit and download.

bookshelf.title: Bookshelf
bookshelf.p1: Finished or abandoned reading goals appear as books on the "Bookshelf" screen, separate from the goal list. Finished and abandoned books sit on separate shelves so you can tell them apart at a glance. Selecting a book lets you review its bibliographic info, records (list of recall entries), growth notes, and retrospective report together on a single tabbed screen.
bookshelf.p2: Putting a book away just hides it, the same as "Archive" on the goal list. "Return to shelf" brings it back right away. Deleting the book itself shows the same confirmation screen as the goal list.

resources.title: Study environment settings
resources.p1: Register the "study time slots" available for studying (name, start/end time, environment tags, days applied). Continuous time is calculated automatically from the start and end times. Time slots that satisfy each material's required continuous time and environment are assigned automatically. "Allocation status" lets you check the allocated and remaining time for each goal within each time slot, and shows a warning if shortening or deleting a time slot causes an allocation to exceed capacity (saving itself is not blocked).
resources.p2: "Default day type settings" lets you set the default (plan day / buffer day) for each day of the week and whether to treat public holidays as buffer days. "Day boundary time" lets you set when the date changes over (e.g. treating late-night study as the previous day). "Allocation status" lets you check time allocation and unallocated remainder by day of week, environment, and goal.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.p1: The monthly calendar shows each day's status (not entered / progress only / reported) along with auxiliary markers such as exam dates, exam periods, and load adjustments. Clicking a date takes you to the daily report, progress-only, or view screen depending on that day's status (an unreported previous day shows a choice of how to register, 2+ days ago is progress-only, and an already-reported day opens the view screen).
calendar.p2: "Change day type" lets you override that day's type (plan day / buffer day / excluded day) individually. "Clear override" reverts it to the default.
calendar.p3: If you have 2 or more active goals, a goal tab appears at the top of the screen, letting you select one goal at a time (the same approach as the daily report screen). Auxiliary markers (exam dates, reading due dates, etc.) show only the selected goal's data. Background colors and recorded status aren't tied to a goal, so they're shared regardless of which goal tab is selected.

dailyReport.title: Daily report / Progress only / View daily report
dailyReport.p1: On the "Daily report" screen, for each material scheduled today, you enter the time spent per time slot, amount completed, cycle, and quality metric, and write a diary entry (what you learned/understood today). After getting feedback through AI dialogue, finalize with "Finalize report." Time spent starts out pre-filled from your resource allocation settings; change it only if your actual time differs (the change applies only for that day and doesn't affect your resource allocation settings). If you studied in a time slot you haven't allocated, you can record it with "Add another time slot." Note that leaving this screen before finalizing discards your input.
dailyReport.p2: "Progress only" is a simplified version that enters only your results. Input fields appear for each active category (certification exam, reading, work), and a single "Register" records them all at once (a category that's already been reported won't show, since it can't be changed). Time spent can be left blank (leave every time slot field empty), in which case that day is excluded from effective speed calculations. There is no diary or AI dialogue.
dailyReport.p3: "View daily report" shows a finalized past report read-only, letting you check your results, diary, and AI dialogue history, and add comments only.
dailyReport.p4: If you have an active reading goal, the same screen shows a separate "Today's reading recall" field and AI dialogue, apart from the certification exam ones (only the recall text is required; numeric results are optional). The only page field is "Current page" — you don't need to enter how many pages you read that day. Current page is used only for the on-screen progress display and isn't evaluated by the AI. Reading's AI dialogue is saved as a separate conversation from the certification exam's.
dailyReport.p5: If you have an active work goal, the same screen shows separate work record fields and AI dialogue, apart from certification exam and reading. Enter today's work record text per project (there are no fields for time spent or daily quota), then finalize after the AI dialogue. The list of registered team members is also shown on the same screen (view only; add/edit from the "Project info" tab on the goal details screen).

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.p1: Select a goal from the goal tab at the top of the screen to view various analyses in tabs that depend on the goal's type (certification exam / reading / work). Closed goals can also be selected for retrospection. Archived goals are hidden by default; check "Show archived" to add them to the goal tab.
analytics.p2: A certification exam goal has 7 tabs: "Quality trend" (quality metric trend by cycle and granularity, with a passing criteria line), "Progress" (comparison of actual vs. plan line), "Forecast" (forecast completion date and deviation from due date, per material), "Effective speed" (effective speed trend by cycle), "Gantt chart" (planned period per material), "Replan history" (history of quota changes), and "Growth notes" (history of AI daily report feedback).
analytics.p3: A reading goal has 2 tabs, "Reading log" (list of daily recall records) and "Growth notes"; a work goal also has 2 tabs, "Work log" (list of daily work records) and "Growth notes" (since they don't use quota, effective speed, or similar calculations). "Growth notes" shows the history of AI daily report feedback addressed to the selected goal. History generated before goals were separated by feature (pre-migration) is shown as "Unassigned," and can be manually assigned to a goal from the dropdown.

examAndExport.title: Register exam results / Knowledge export
examAndExport.p1: Before marking a goal as complete, register the pass/fail result, score, evaluation, and notes for each subject (you cannot complete it until results are in). Completing the goal takes you to the knowledge export screen. The retrospective report is created when you press "Generate" on that screen.
examAndExport.p2: On the knowledge export screen, you can review and regenerate the retrospective report, check your study summary (total time spent, days studied, report rate, replan count, latest quality achieved), and choose export items (goal overview, material composition, study volume summary, progress history, quality metric trend, replan history, weekly summaries, recap themes, diary entries, AI dialogue history, exam results, retrospective report) to export as Markdown/JSON. Progress history also includes the time breakdown by time slot. Enabling "Anonymize" excludes diary entries and regenerates the weekly summaries / retrospective report as an anonymized version before exporting.
examAndExport.p3: For reading goals, there's a "Mark as finished" action instead of exam results (in the goal's action area). Completing it takes you to the knowledge export screen. The completion report is created when you press "Generate" on that screen. An abandoned reading goal can be completed after resuming and finishing it.

aiConnection.title: Settings — AI connection
aiConnection.p1: AI integration requires NewtonX's "Connection URL (tenant host)" and "Personal Access Token (PAT)." Enter the Host in its full form including the domain, like `xxx.newton-x.net` (a company name or abbreviation alone cannot resolve the connection). The `xxx` part differs by affiliation (Seraku in-house staff: `seraku.newton-x.net`; Seraku on-site staff: `seraku-ex.newton-x.net`; Seraku Business Solutions: `bs-seraku.newton-x.net`; AND Think: `andthink.newton-x.net`). If yours isn't listed, use the `xxx` part of the URL you normally use to sign in to NewtonX, `https://xxx.newton-x.net/login`. Please issue your own PAT from NewtonX's web app account screen (this app cannot issue one for you).
aiConnection.p2: After entering the Host and PAT and pressing "Check connection," the app applies them to the development kit (NewtonX ADK) settings, actually tries communicating with the AI platform (fetching the assistant list), and shows either "Connected successfully" or a failure reason, along with "Authenticated"/"Not authenticated," based on the result. This is where you'll notice any mistakes in the Host format or PAT. If network conditions change afterward, you may still see errors again later, for example during daily report AI dialogue.
aiConnection.p3: After authenticating, you assign the assistant to use — from a list, no need to type an identifier by hand — for each of 13 purposes: daily report feedback, weekly summary, today's message, retrospective report, each of their reading and work variants, the work AI evaluation report, and the help question assistant. Each purpose already has a default assistant preselected to match its task characteristics, so in most cases you can leave it as-is. Only change it from the list if you want to use a different assistant.

settingsOther.title: Settings — Thresholds, prompt degradation, display, logs, prompt templates
settingsOther.p1: "Thresholds": sets the warning ratio (shows a warning banner when your quota exceeds the plan by this ratio) and the forced replan overrun days (forces a replan prompt once the deviation exceeds this many days).
settingsOther.p2: "Prompt degradation": sets the character limit for prompts sent to the AI, how many weeks of weekly summaries to inject into the prompt, and the threshold (number of finalized records) below which the AI is prompted to ask from multiple perspectives for users with few records. Prompts exceeding the limit are degraded (shortened) in stages, in this order: weekly summaries → aggregated material info → dialogue history → diary entries.
settingsOther.p3: "Display": sets the display language (Japanese / English), theme (follow system setting / light / dark), accent color, font size, and the default analytics granularity (daily / weekly / monthly). Changing the language reloads the page. NewtonX feedback is also generated in Japanese or English according to this setting.
settingsOther.p4: "Logs": sets whether to save AI communication logs, and if so, how long to retain them (in days).
settingsOther.p5: "Prompt templates": lets you edit, and reset to default, the actual prompt text sent to the AI, for each of 15 purposes (daily report feedback, weekly summary, today's message, retrospective report, each reading and work variant, the work AI evaluation report, recap classification/body generation, and the help question assistant). See the "Prompt template placeholders" section below for the list of `{{variable_name}}` placeholders available when editing (only the main purposes are listed).
settingsOther.p6: "System info": from the "Go to system info" link in the top right, you can check the app version, the list of libraries used, and export diagnostic logs.

desktop.title: App startup and shutdown, recording reminder notifications
desktop.p1: When you start Michinari, the window opens in your browser, and the app itself stays running in the notification area in the bottom right of your screen (where icons sit to the left of the clock). No black console window is shown. If you can't find the icon, click the "^" button in the notification area to reveal hidden icons.
desktop.p2: Clicking Michinari's icon in the notification area opens the window. Right-clicking the icon shows an "Open Michinari" / "Quit" menu. Closing the browser tab doesn't quit the app. To quit, choose "Quit" from this menu. Choosing "Quit" waits for any in-progress save to finish before stopping safely.
desktop.p3: In "Desktop & notifications" on the Settings screen, you can toggle whether the browser window opens on startup. If off, open it manually from the tray icon. Turning on "Launch automatically at Windows startup" (in the same place) makes Michinari wait in the tray when you sign in (off by default).
desktop.p4: Turning on "Send recording reminder notifications" shows a notification at the time you set (default 21:00), but only if that day's record isn't done yet. Clicking the notification opens that day's daily report screen in your browser. No notification is sent for a day already recorded (whether progress-only or fully reported), or a day marked as excluded on the calendar. On buffer days, the notification uses a lighter message for rest days.
desktop.p5: Notifications only work while Michinari is running (no separate background program is installed on your PC). If Michinari wasn't running at the set time, that day's notification won't fire. If notifications don't appear, check that Michinari is allowed to notify you under Windows Settings → System → Notifications.

promptVariables.title: Prompt template placeholder list
promptVariables.p1: Writing `{{variable_name}}` in a prompt template's text causes the system to automatically substitute the actual value when sending it to the AI. The variables available for each purpose are as follows (only the variables in this list can be used in the template editor).

variables.goal_summary: Goal name, subject composition, exam date per subject, days remaining
variables.material_status: Per material: total amount, planned cycles, current cycle, remaining amount, due date, daily quota, required speed, effective speed, forecast completion date, deviation days
variables.slot_summary: Today's available time slots and their material assignments
variables.today_logs: Today's results by material (time spent, amount completed, cycle, quality metric)
variables.diary_body: Previous diary entry (legacy input; empty for new entries)
variables.perspective_suggestion: Extra instruction prompting users with few records to be asked from multiple perspectives (inserted only when below the threshold)

variables.week_logs: Daily results within the week (including cycle)
variables.week_diaries: Diary entries within the week (actions/thoughts, what was learned)
variables.week_metrics: Weekly aggregates (total time spent, total amount completed, average quality metric, days reported, buffer day usage)
variables.anonymize: Anonymization instruction (inserted only when generating an anonymized version)

variables.progress_summary: Progress rate and current cycle per material
variables.recent_activity: Report status and results over the last 7 days

variables.goal_summary: Exam name, study period, subject composition
variables.material_summary: Per material: total amount, planned cycles, actual cycles, time spent
variables.overall_metrics: Total time spent, days studied, report rate, buffer day usage rate, replan count
variables.quality_trend: Quality metric trend (by cycle, aggregated monthly)
variables.replan_history: Replan history (date, reason, quota before/after, remaining amount and days at that time)
variables.anonymize: Anonymization instruction (inserted only when generating an anonymized version)

variables.book_summary: Title, author, target completion date, days remaining
variables.recent_recalls: Recall records from the last several days
variables.perspective_suggestion: Extra instruction prompting readers with few records to be asked from multiple perspectives (inserted only when below the threshold)

variables.work_summary: Project name, client/project name, expected work content, days elapsed since start
variables.recent_work_logs: Work records from the last several days
variables.perspective_suggestion: Extra instruction prompting users with few records to be asked from multiple perspectives (inserted only when below the threshold)

variables.anonymize: Anonymization instruction (inserted only when generating an anonymized version)

variables.weekly_summaries: Generated weekly summaries (for long periods, used in place of raw logs for earlier periods)
variables.reading_logs: Recall records (raw logs) for periods without a weekly summary yet
variables.anonymize: Anonymization instruction (inserted only when generating an anonymized version)

variables.work_summary: Project name, client/project name, expected work content, start date
variables.target_month_or_period: Target month (monthly report) / target half (semiannual review)
variables.target_goal_text: The "goal for next period" set last time
variables.weekly_summaries: Generated weekly summaries (for long periods, used in place of raw logs for earlier periods)
variables.month_or_period_logs: Work records (raw logs) for periods without a weekly summary yet
variables.anonymize: Anonymization instruction (inserted only when generating an anonymized version)

variables.member_summary: The evaluated member's name, gender, and traits/personality (if registered)
variables.feedback_history: This project's daily report feedback history (the AI's responses)
variables.work_logs: Work records for the target period

variables.existing_themes: List of existing theme names (for classification)
variables.entries: Report text to classify (diary / recall records, for classification)
variables.new_entries: New report text to merge in this time (for body generation)
variables.body_max_chars: Character limit for the theme body (for body generation)

variables.help_body: Help text relevant to the question
variables.question: The user's question text
variables.nonce: A random value to prevent delimiter spoofing (used to verify output)

dataManagement.title: Data management
dataManagement.p1: The "Data management" screen (reached from Settings) lets you export/import the entire database file, and create, list, and restore backups. Both import and restore overwrite existing data, so a confirmation dialog appears before running them.

faq.title: FAQ / troubleshooting
faq.q1: Where do I get a Personal Access Token (PAT)?
faq.a1: Please issue it yourself from NewtonX's web app account screen. This app cannot issue a PAT for you.
faq.q2: The Settings screen shows "Authenticated," but I can't fetch the assistant list.
faq.a2: Please check the format of the "Connection URL (tenant host)" (see the "Settings — AI connection" section for the value for each affiliation). The "Authenticated" status in the authentication state only confirms that a PAT is set — it's separate from whether you can actually connect to the AI platform. If the Host isn't in full domain form, like `xxx.newton-x.net`, an organization name or abbreviation alone cannot resolve the connection, causing communication such as fetching the assistant list to fail.
faq.q3: AI-related actions show "An error occurred with the AI connection" or "The AI connection timed out."
faq.a3: There's a problem communicating with the AI platform. Please wait a while and try again. If it keeps happening, check the Host, PAT, and timeout settings on the Settings screen.
faq.q4: I accidentally broke my data. Can I undo it?
faq.a4: Go to "Data management" on the Settings screen, select an existing backup, and run "Restore." If you hadn't created a backup, you can't return to the previous state. We recommend creating backups regularly.
faq.q5: What happens if I leave the screen without finalizing a daily report?
faq.a5: Your unfinalized input (results, diary, AI dialogue) is kept within the app even if you move to another screen, and is restored when you return to the daily report screen. However, closing or reloading the browser tab discards the content (a standard browser confirmation dialog appears right before that action). If you leave the app open for a long time, we recommend not postponing finalizing for too long, in case the tab gets closed unintentionally.
faq.q6: The black console window I used to see in an older version doesn't appear anymore.
faq.a6: The app no longer shows a black console window. It now runs in the notification area as a tray icon. To quit, right-click that icon and choose "Quit."
